name: Credentials and password-manager exports
one_line: A safety-only template for password-manager and browser exports, recovery-code sheets, private authentication keys, client-key containers, password-reset records, and recognized encrypted credential vaults. It detects enough structure to protect or represent the material, stores no credential values, creates no automatic folder depth, and never forces open an unreadable container.
design_cite: 00 supplies both the safety trigger and the residual home: "A scanned passport, tax statement, medical document, authentication key, or account record should enter a protected state immediately." It also says: "Protected Records may represent sensitive isolated material such as passport scans, medical documents, account statements, visas, legal forms, or credentials; it should normally remain local-only and must not cause filenames or content to be exposed in model prompts."
node_test_note: KEEP. The Identity schema's default recognition is a broad safety union across civil documents, immigration records, contacts, keys, credential exports and opaque containers. This row has a narrower and operationally distinct boundary: it consumes the dedicated R2 credential/key observation families, distinguishes private from public key material, recognizes password-export archive structure, separates live secrets from configuration that merely references them, and owns the unresolved exact-format treatment of opaque credential vaults. Its dimension order is necessarily the same empty list because Identity has no legal fields, but its privacy rule is sharper than the schema default: an authentication secret is never a fact, label, excerpt, preview or candidate branch value, and an unreadable object is never opened to make the template fire.

deterministic: the observation conjunction already owned by R2 rule det-credential-password-export: a recognized credential header or structured-key set together with populated records beneath it. This node consumes the rule family and its evidence references; it does not duplicate the header vocabulary, patterns or injected row count. The populated secret values trigger protection but are never facts and never dossier content.

the observation conjunction already owned by R2 rule det-credential-2fa-backup-codes: explicit backup/recovery context and a code-grid region in the same text unit. A heading or a grid by itself does not fire. The code spans are authentication secrets and remain local; the node needs only the cited heading and region observations to recognize the situation.

the observation conjunction already owned by R2 rule det-auth-key-material: a private-key armor marker and its matching encoded body in one structured-text unit. The rule distinguishes PRIVATE or ENCRYPTED PRIVATE material from PUBLIC KEY and CERTIFICATE material. This row consumes the fired observation family and never copies the key body.

a 1Password 1PUX archive manifest whose member layout includes export.attributes, export.data and the files subtree, read without extracting members to disk. The layout is the evidence; a .1pux extension or a filename containing 1Password is not. The format is documented as an unencrypted export, so recognition immediately invokes protection even though the normal scan reads only the manifest.

a dedicated, explicitly approved metadata-only parser reporting an exact credential-vault format signature plus that format's outer structural markers, such as a valid KDBX database header. This is a PROPOSED protection-only signal required by the roster's opaque_binary ownership; generic encryption never satisfies it. Current R2 instead leaves unreadable KDBX material unclassified, so the disagreement is recorded in open_question rather than hidden.

a dedicated PKCS #12 parser reporting a valid PFX container together with a keyBag or shrouded-key-bag type in safely readable outer structure. RFC 7292 allows certificates and other material in the same container, so a .p12/.pfx extension or PFX wrapper alone is never enough; certificate-only material stays outside this template.

a locally observed recovery-phrase or mnemonic heading together with a structured word-list region. This is a PROPOSED R2 rule family, not a pattern authored here: R2 currently has backup-code and private-key rules but no wallet mnemonic rule. Until that catalogue gap is resolved, the observation may raise protective review but may not silently become a normalized fact or a cloud-model excerpt.
needs_llm: deciding whether an unlabelled photograph or screenshot is a handwritten account-recovery secret rather than a word puzzle, quotation, language exercise or ordinary note. For this safety row, needs_llm means a local model or an explicitly authorized path after P7; raw OCR and suspected secret spans never enter a cloud dossier, and abstention remains correct.

distinguishing a manually maintained account-access inventory from a bookmarks list, signup tracker or subscription inventory when the exact R2 credential-header conjunction is absent. A local model may interpret headings and column roles, but it may not read secret values to answer the question and may not mint service, username or credential-type facts.

distinguishing a genuine saved password-reset record from generic security guidance, a phishing example, a simulated-awareness exercise or quoted documentation when native sender/subject structure and body language conflict. The model judges document role, not link safety, sender authenticity or whether a token remains valid.

judging whether a readable mixed archive manifest represents one credential backup kit or merely co-locates unrelated configuration, certificates and account records. The manifest is a candidate-set clue; the model may propose reviewable membership with citations and may not inspect or unpack protected members.

deciding whether a partially redacted export still functions as a credential store when password cells have been removed but password-manager structure, login records and recovery material remain. A redacted sample is not automatically safe, and an empty password column is not automatically a credential store.

resolving multilingual recovery or password-manager labels when structured slots are present but the local rule catalogue does not support the language. The model path remains closed to default cloud use; if no permitted local interpretation exists, the safe result is protection plus abstention.
never_alone: a filename or extension: Passwords.csv, vault.kdbx, id_ed25519, secret.key, client.p12, credentials.zip and recovery-codes.txt are claims, not meanings. 00 says unreadable files must not gain a purpose from their filename alone, and the real MIME type, signature or content structure must decide.
source_type = opaque_binary, archive, spreadsheet, code_structured, text_document, image, ocr or email. file_kind plausibility is routing evidence and never activation by itself.

encryption, password protection, unreadability or high entropy. A locked archive can hold holiday photos, legal records, source code or anything else; without an exact recognized credential format it is Unsupported or Encrypted, not this template.

a long opaque string or high-entropy-looking value. Checksums, compressed data, identifiers, ciphertext, build artefacts and random test fixtures share the shape. R2's labelled conjunctions own secret detection.

the words password, secret, token, key, credential, identity, certificate, recovery or vault in prose, source identifiers, filenames or folder names. Password policies, cryptography textbooks, professional credentials, public certificates and data-recovery guides are false friends.

a public key, certificate, certificate-signing request or key fingerprint. Public material may be paired with a private key in a reviewed group, but PUBLIC KEY or CERTIFICATE structure alone is not an authentication secret and cannot activate this template.
a service name, URL, username, email address, login-form screenshot or account number. Those observations occur in bookmarks, statements, contacts and documentation; none proves a stored secret.
a credential-shaped header with no populated credential records. R2 explicitly treats an empty password column as a template or signup tracker rather than sufficient evidence.

a configuration file that contains a secret-shaped slot name or refers to an external credential helper. A tool configuration may trigger Identity protection for a live value while remaining the code.dotfiles-environment situation; the slot name does not make the whole file a credential store.

a repository, home-directory or .ssh-directory location. Position may retrieve likely neighbors, but a sibling private key does not turn config, known_hosts or a public-key file into secret material, and a project root does not license reorganization of its descendants.

membership in a download session, backup directory, accepted vault group or crypto-account neighborhood. 00 says: "A session should never be treated as proof of topic", and group membership never copies a credential conclusion onto a sparse member.
missing EXIF, dense OCR or display-shaped dimensions as proof that an image is a recovery-code screenshot. 00 requires positive capture evidence and allows conflicting signals to end in abstention.

an outer archive name, even credentials.zip or vault-backup.zip. Only a readable manifest or an exact dedicated container parser can contribute structural evidence, and member facts never copy onto the archive.

a date or version-shaped token in an export name. It may support a universal version family after independent comparison, but it is not a credential fact, an account identity or proof that one export supersedes another.

a neighboring recognized credential as proof that an unreadable object contains another credential. The graph may retrieve the object for review, but 00: "The graph does not automatically copy those missing facts onto sparse files."

grouping_reasons: one password-manager export bundle: an outer 1PUX or ZIP manifest, its data member and attachment subtree. The archive remains one protected candidate set and the normal scan never extracts its members to disk.

one vault across exact duplicates, safe backups and exports. duplicate_family and version_family are universal facts; a date-shaped filename does not decide which copy is current, and no duplicate is deleted automatically.

one authentication-key set: a private key, its derived public key and an issued certificate, but only when a local cryptographic parser can verify the correspondence without exposing the private material. A filename stem or shared directory is insufficient, and an encrypted key is never unlocked merely to form the group.

one account-recovery kit whose independently read members share explicit provider and recovery context: backup-code sheet, recovery setup confirmation and reset notice. Membership is reviewable context, not a provider, username, status or credential-type fact copied onto every member.

one credential migration event represented by a source export, a destination import report and an explicitly labelled completion notice. A bounded download session may retrieve the candidates but cannot prove the event or propagate membership.

one protected singleton. Credential-bearing material is useful to surface for safety even when no normal multi-file group exists; the proposal is protection or representation, not an exposed one-file folder.

one mixed code or crypto neighborhood in which a credential file remains protected while Code or Finance facts stand on their own members. Multi-membership never weakens the safety policy and never makes secret values into shared group facts.

one unreadable object manually attached by the user to a credential group. The attachment records user-confirmed membership while the object's own purpose and contents remain unknown; no group label is copied back as a fact.

template.why: Empty by binding contract and by privacy. Identity is a D1/PR-6 field-less safety placeholder, so service, site, account, username, holder, credential type, key type, provider, expiry and recovery method are not legal fields and cannot appear in dimension_order. The safety purpose is explicit: "Finance, identity, medical, and legal material should be implemented first as safety domains, meaning the system detects and protects them before any cloud or automated placement decision is allowed." A path such as Provider/Username/Recovery Codes would disclose both service usage and account-recovery capability even while file contents remain encrypted. The current recommendation is therefore no automatic branch at all: leave the object in place or represent it in one redacted Protected Records area, with any depth created only by explicit user action after privacy policy. This is not time-first; export dates support review and version evidence, not organizational identity.

collides_with.signal: Reciprocal. The words identity, credential, certificate and key can occur on both an official bearer document and authentication material. The discriminating evidence is the document's function and structure: a government issuer plus bearer or civil-status slots makes the core-document situation; a private-key block, password-export schema, recovery-code set, key-bearing PFX or exact credential-vault format makes this situation. A certificate label, person name, identifier or shared filename decides neither. Fixtures: Certificate of Naturalization.pdf versus client-auth.p12 and id_ed25519.

Reciprocal. A credential-shaped slot name or opaque value can appear in both machine configuration and a credential store. The discriminating evidence is what the file itself is: a tool configuration that contains or references a secret remains the dotfiles/environment situation while Identity safety co-activates; a file whose whole structure is private key material, populated credential records or recovery codes is this situation. Directory position and the shared word secret decide neither; when unresolved, protection wins without manufacturing credential-group membership. Fixtures: .env.production and an SSH config stay on the Code side; id_ed25519 and Passwords.csv stay here.

Reciprocal. A wallet-tool name, venue name, account identifier or encrypted container can sit beside both holdings records and self-custody secrets. The discriminating evidence is function: labelled period, balance, amount, holdings or transaction structure reports on assets and belongs to finance.crypto-assets; a recovery phrase, private key, key-bearing keystore or credential-vault structure grants access and belongs here. The same venue or wallet filename stem must never count for both. Fixtures: Exchange Account Statement 2026-Q1.pdf versus recovery phrase backup.jpg and Personal.kdbx.

Reciprocal. The word credential, a person's name, an issuer and an identifier can support either reading, and credentials.zip is a live outer-name fixture. The discriminating evidence is authority versus access: professional standing granted by a board, membership body or certifier belongs to career.credentials-licenses; a password, recovery code, authentication key or credential-store structure belongs here. A certificate or identifier alone activates neither. Fixture: credentials.zip containing a nursing licence and membership confirmation.

falls_through_to.why: The primary home or representation for recognized credential-bearing material without an accepted protected group. 00 defines it directly: "Protected Records may represent sensitive isolated material such as passport scans, medical documents, account statements, visas, legal forms, or credentials; it should normally remain local-only and must not cause filenames or content to be exposed in model prompts." A protected singleton remains useful even without a normal multi-file group.

The home—or safer representation without moving—for a generic locked archive, unreadable key container, damaged vault or unknown binary whose purpose cannot be established safely. 00 says: "Unsupported or Encrypted may hold—or, more safely, represent without moving—password-protected archives, unreadable documents, damaged files, and unknown formats." Exact known credential-container recognition versus this residual is the open merge fork, never resolved from a filename.

For a readable account-access inventory or partially redacted export whose role is partly understood but does not satisfy an approved credential rule. The file remains protected if P7 found a secret; review does not license a model to inspect it.

For public password, cryptography or account-security guidance that uses credential vocabulary but contains no personal account-access material and has no active project association. Fixture: Password Security Policy.pdf.

For a positively identified screenshot such as an empty login page when no credential record, accepted project or account association exists. Missing EXIF alone never selects it. Fixture: Login page.png.

For a durable public certificate or public-key record that does not contain private authentication material and has no accepted code or credential group. Fixture: id_ed25519.pub when correspondence to a private key is not verified.

sensitivity_why: The catalogue value is only potentially_sensitive; no P7 handling class is authored here. Operationally, this row sits at the sharpest end of that value because 00 says: "A scanned passport, tax statement, medical document, authentication key, or account record should enter a protected state immediately." It further requires: "Paths, complete extracted text, OCR output, file hashes, image EXIF, GPS, user edits, group memberships, and raw sensitive values should remain local." R2's authentication_secret identifier class therefore drops the whole secret span and keeps it always local; this node never stores a password, recovery code, private key, token, mnemonic, username or service account as a fact. Protected filenames, previews and raw content remain out of ordinary summaries and default cloud prompts, and an opaque object is never decrypted merely to improve classification.
open_question: NEEDS JOSEPH on one concrete merge boundary. The roster says this row owns opaque_binary credential vaults, while current R2 says binary keystores and KDBX databases with no extractable text cannot fire its key/password-export rules and remain unreadable/unclassified. Should an exact, dedicated metadata-only format identification—valid KDBX header, or PFX plus a key-bag type—activate Identity protection and Protected Records without decrypting content, or must every unreadable object remain Unsupported or Encrypted until the user confirms its purpose? This row recommends exact credential-format evidence may activate protection, generic encryption may not, and neither permits opening the object. R2 also lacks a wallet-mnemonic rule even though finance.crypto-assets routes recovery phrases here; R2 should own that vocabulary if Joseph accepts it. Independently, the inherited protected-depth question is sharper for credentials: even provider or account labels in folder paths disclose where and how the user authenticates, so this row recommends no automatic depth until a product-wide privacy policy explicitly permits it.
